criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The mission concept is thoroughly articulated. Goals, objectives, and preliminary requirements are clearly quantified and directly traced to Australian stakeholders (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM) with relevant literature citations.

evidence.quote: Mission goal. Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: The project plan includes a clear Gantt chart, detailed task breakdowns, an explicit rationale relating task order to orbital physics, a robust risk/contingency matrix, and tabulated information sources.

evidence.quote: The order follows the mission: the imaging requirements (objectives 1 and 2) fix the orbit altitude and local time

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Preliminary hand calculations for a 600 km sun-synchronous orbit are completely correct. The interpretation demonstrates strong engineering insight by identifying the coverage-versus-resolution trade-off.

evidence.quote: Interpretation: the reef is up to about 250 km wide, so a 60 km swath needs at least five neighbouring passes

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report is professionally written and structured. Tables and figures are neatly formatted and captioned. In-text citations correctly match the reference list.

evidence.quote: Figure 1: Project Gantt chart, Weeks 2 to 10 (gold = completed, blue = planned, red lines = report deadlines).

overall: An exemplary preliminary report. The mission concept directly addresses Australian environmental monitoring, the project plan includes thoughtful contingencies, and the preliminary orbital calculations demonstrate excellent technical competence.

feedback.summary: You have produced an exemplary preliminary report that thoroughly establishes your mission concept. Your clear alignment with Australian stakeholders (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM), robust project plan, and accurate preliminary orbital calculations set an excellent foundation. To carry this standard into your final mission design, maintain this rigour when expanding your trade-offs, detailed subsystem designs, and simulation work.
next_steps: Leverage your identified coverage-versus-resolution trade-off from 'Preliminary Progress' to guide detailed payload and swath selection in Part 2.
Progress your Gantt chart (Figure 1) tasks by initiating software simulations to validate your 600 km sun-synchronous orbit hand calculations.
Continue engaging with requirements from GBRMPA and AIMS as you transition preliminary mission goals into detailed subsystem specifications.

criteria.C1: You achieved an Accomplished level by providing a clear, quantified description of mission goals, objectives, and preliminary requirements in 'Mission Concept & Rationale'. Citing literature and explicitly linking functions to users like AIMS, GBRMPA, and CSIRO was excellent. For the final submission, maintain this standard by flowing these stakeholder requirements directly into technical subsystem specifications.
criteria.C2: You achieved the Accomplished level in 'Project Plan' by presenting a detailed task breakdown, tabulated sources, and a robust risk/contingency matrix. Linking task sequencing in Figure 1 to orbital physics provided strong justification. To maintain this level in the full assignment, track your progress against planned contingency triggers and document any baseline schedule variations.
criteria.C3: In 'Preliminary Progress', you achieved the Accomplished level with flawless hand calculations for a 600 km sun-synchronous orbit. Your interpretation demonstrated mature engineering insight by identifying the coverage-versus-resolution trade-off across the 250 km reef width. To maintain this standard for the final report, build on these calculations using orbital simulation tools to validate ground tracks and revisit rates.
criteria.C4: You met the Accomplished standard with professional report presentation. The structure is logical, language is appropriate, and captions such as Figure 1 are clear and informative. In-text citations also matched your reference list correctly. To maintain this level in your final report, continue applying consistent formatting to more complex technical diagrams, data tables, and expanded reference sections.
